newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein mourns Rabin as "man of courage".
newsitem.headline: King Hussein mourns Rabin as "man of courage".

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein paid tribute on Thursday to his slain "friend and colleague" Yitzhak Rabin, Israel's prime minister who was gunned down by a right-wing Jew a year ago.
The king, speaking on the Jewish anniversary of Rabin's death, said his assassination was a loss which would be felt in the Middle East "for a long, long time to come."

"To me it was the loss of a friend and colleague," the monarch told a joint news conference with French President Jacque Chirac. "He was a man of courage not in the field of battle only, but in the field of the battle for peace."

King Hussein, who signed a peace treaty two years ago with Rabin which formally ended a 46-year state of war between Jordan and Israel, praised Rabin as "a man whose word could be taken seriously at any time".
"So when he, as God's will was, left the scene, the loss was felt as of that moment," the king said. "I think that it will be felt for a long, long time."

Ties between Jordan and Israel, the closest of any Arab country with the Jewish state, took a turn for the worse last month when the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near the Moslem and Jewish holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem.
"Hopes and aspirations for a better future...are confronted by the lack of vision of some, or the intent of others to destroy all that we have built," King Hussein said.
